note: The repository's mods folder. Jars are dropped into mods/jars/ by hand (they are third-party binaries and git ignores them) and this file describes them, so the launcher can offer the right ones for a version and a mode. tools/launchplan.py reads this, checks every jar is really there, and stages the jars into the deployed site as site/mods/. Only add a mod you are licensed to redistribute.

mods.name: Hello WebMC
mods.note: Built from mods/examples/hello-webmc by tools/build_mods.py. Proves the loader's own mod door: no Minecraft classes, only the loader's API. It has to be built before it can be offered - a jar is never committed.

mods.name: Hello Fabric
mods.note: a Fabric mod built from mods/examples/hello-fabric. On a version with a real JVM it is started by Fabric Loader at play time; on a compiled version the bake applies it before the compile. The one kind of mod that cannot work anywhere is one with native libraries.

mods.name: Hello Mixin
mods.note: A mixin: its code is merged into the client's own class files at build time, which is the only way a mixin can work in an ahead-of-time client. Built from mods/examples/hello-mixin by tools/build_mods.py, and baked the same way - opt in with a build tag such as build-1.21.11+hello-fabric,hello-mixin. MIXINS.md lists the mixin shapes that are applied and the ones that are refused by name.

mods.name: Meteor Client
mods.note: The real thing, from meteorclient.com (its GitHub releases carry no jar). Committed rather than downloaded because GPL-3.0 allows redistribution and the build has to read it: 1340 classes, 233 mixin classes across six configs, an access widener, and its own copies of the Fabric API modules with a nested-jar layout. The bake applies entrypoints and a subset of mixins (MIXINS.md), so this is the honest test of how far that gets - the build log names every part it cannot apply instead of shipping a client that quietly ignores the mod.

mods.name: Fabric API
mods.note: The real Fabric API, compiled into the client by the bake rather than shimmed member by member. 43 modules: 18 need nothing, 17 need one named adapter (files->OPFS, threads->scheduler, LWJGL->the port's natives), 8 are desktop-only and are left out with the reason. Redistributed under Apache-2.0 (see CREDITS.md).

mods.name: Sodium
mods.note: The renderer of the Fabric world, downloaded from Modrinth. Its 77 mixin classes all apply in the build-time merge.

mods.name: Lithium
mods.note: Server-side game logic optimisations that a client build carries too; 253 of its 262 mixins apply, and the rest are named in the build log.

mods.name: Mod Menu
mods.note: A list of what is loaded. A good first mod to bake: it shows the other mods, so 'did it work' is visible in the client.
